703333.t: From Proto-Hellenic *dékə, from Proto-Indo-European *déḱm̥. Cognates include Sanskrit दश (dáśa), Latin decem, Old Armenian տասն (tasn) and Old English tīen (English ten).

703353.t: Traditionally derived from Proto-Indo-European *der-drew-om with dissimilation, reduplicated from *dóru (“tree”), but this type of reduplication is highly atypical, so the formation must be regarded as uncertain.

703360.t: From Proto-Hellenic *deksiwós, from Proto-Indo-European *deḱs-. Cognate with Sanskrit दक्षिण (dákṣiṇa) and Latin dexter.

703394.t: From Proto-Hellenic *déyō, from Proto-Indo-European *dh₁yéti (“to bind”), from *deh₁- (“to bind”). Cognates include Sanskrit द्यति (dyati), Avestan 𐬥𐬍𐬛𐬌𐬌𐬁𐬙𐬄𐬨 (nīdiiātąm) and Albanian duaj.

703303.t: From Proto-Hellenic *dḗ, from Proto-Indo-European *de (deictic particle). See also δή (dḗ).

703395.t: From Proto-Hellenic *dḗ, from Proto-Indo-European *de (“instrumental particle”). See also δέ (dé).

703379.t: From Proto-Hellenic *déspotis, an original phrase from Proto-Indo-European *déms pótis (“master of the house”), from *dṓm (“house”), whence also Ancient Greek δόμος (dómos, “house”); and *pótis (“master”), whence also Ancient Greek πόσις (pósĭs,…

703389.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *dews-? Proto-Indo-European *-teros Ancient Greek -τερος (-teros) Ancient Greek δεύτερος Uncertain.

703328.t: From Proto-Indo-European *dweynós, from *dwey- (“fear”); equivalent to δει- (dei-), the root of δείδω (deídō), + -νος (-nos). Compare δέος (déos).

703362.t: For *δϝέϳος (*dwéjos), the σ-stem abstract noun formed from Proto-Indo-European *dwey- (“to fear”), whence also δεινός (deinós). Cognate to Old Armenian երկն (erkn), Latin dīrus.

703366.t: From Proto-Hellenic *dérō, from Proto-Indo-European *der- (“to tear, tear apart”).

703382.t: Probably a combination of demonstrative Proto-Indo-European *de, whence also the enclitic -δε (-de, denoting motion towards), + Proto-Indo-European *ure, *uro (“where”), whence Lithuanian aurè, Avestan 𐬀𐬎𐬎𐬀𐬭𐬀 (auuara), Old Armenian ուր (ur), Umbrian 𐌖𐌓𐌖 (uru).

703318.t: Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *dyḗws (“heaven, sky”), thus related to δῆλος (dêlos, “clear, visible”) and cognate to Latin dies

703350.t: According to Beekes, of Semitic origin, related to dalet. (A connection to delta, ultimately from the same Semitic source, has also been proposed.)

703324.t: From Proto-Indo-European *dwey- (“to fear”). Cognate with Ancient Greek δεινός (deinós), Latin dīrus, Old Armenian երկն (erkn).

703331.t: Unknown, with Beekes suspecting Pre-Greek origin.

703313.t: From Proto-Indo-European *dedwóye (“to be afraid”), from *dwey- (“to fear”).

703397.t: From δάκνω (dáknō, “to bite”) and the suffix -μα (-ma).

703302.t: From the aorist stem of δάπτω (dáptō, “to devour, consume”), with a suffix in -ιλ-.

703368.t: From δέω (déō, “to bind, tie, fasten”) + -σις (-sĭs, nominal suffix).

703388.t: From δεύτερος (deúteros, “second”) + νόμος (nómos, “law”) + -ιον (-ion). Translates Biblical Hebrew מִשְׁנֵה הַתּוֹרָה (mišnê hattôrâ).
